outcome: babies being born large for gestational age (LGA)
babies born small for gestational age (SGA)
cohort: The study included 246,670 women aged 18-40 years with BMI >=25 kg/m2 from primary-care practices linked to hospital records in England.
finding: In women with overweight or obesity, a 10-25% weight loss was associated with an increased chance of pregnancy and a reduced risk of gestational diabetes and emergency caesarean section.
mod_finding: Emergency caesarean section was significantly reduced in the weight-loss cohort (OR 0.82; 95% CI 0.71, 0.95; P = 0.008).
birth_weight: Categories of large for gestational age (LGA) and small for gestational age (SGA) were considered.
gest_age: Categories of large for gestational age (LGA), small for gestational age (SGA), and preterm births were considered.
